title: Methodologies and Procedures Employed in the Identification and Quantitation of Lipid Mediators via LC-MS/MS
protocol: Collect blood with anti-coagulant for plasma.
Centrifuge human peripheral blood at 1500 x g for 10 min at room temperature.
Collect plasma.
Store plasma at -80°C until analysis.
Allow the sample to gently thaw on ice.
Prepare methanol containing internal standard (methanol-IS; 500pg in 2mL of methanol/0.5mL of plasma).
Place methanol-IS on ice for 45 min.
Put 1mL of plasma in a 15 mL falcon tube.
Add 4 mL of cold methanol-IS to the plasma sample.
Vortex the mixture for 10 sec.
Keep samples at -20°C for a minimum of 45 min to allow for protein precipitation.
Centrifuge samples at 2000 x g for 10 min at 4°C.
Transfer 2.5 mL of supernatant into round bottom borosilicate tubes.
Store any remaining samples at -80°C.
Place samples in TurboVap LV setting the water bath to 37°C under a gentle flow of Nitrogen gas.
Maintain samples in the evaporator until the final volume of methanol is less than 1 mL.
Place samples on ice.
Turn on and set up Extrahera.
Add new Solid-phase ISOLUTE C18 500 mg/3 mL columns to the rack.
Add new collection tubes.
Fill the solvent stock bottles.
Prime the different solvent feeders.
Turn on the vacuum pump (Adjust the pressure in accordance with the number of samples you plan to run: 3 bar = ¼, 4 bar = ½ and 6 bars = full plate).
Turn on the nitrogen supply (Adjust the pressure in accordance with the number of samples you plan to run: 6 bar = ¼, 8 bar = ½ and 10 bars = full plate).
Empty the waste.
Fill the tips.
Load the samples on Extrahera and start the run.
Wash columns with 3 mL methanol.
Condition columns with 3 mL of water.
Acidify samples by adding pH 3.5 water (HCl) to a final volume of 10 mL.
Load samples onto C18 SPE columns.
Wash columns with 2 mL of water to remove the acid.
Wash columns with 6 mL hexane to remove complex lipids.
Elute mediators into collection tubes using 5 mL methyl formate.
Elute conjugated mediators into separate collection tubes using 5 mL methanol.
Transfer the collected fractions to 15 mL falcon tubes.
Rinse the collection tubes with 1.5 mL methanol and pool with the respective fraction.
Place samples in TurboVap LV setting the water bath to 37°C under a gentle flow of Nitrogen gas.
Place an equal volume to the extracted sample of methanol-IS into a separate 15 mL falcon tube and place it in evaporator with samples.
Check regularly the solvent levels.
When ~95% of the solvent has evaporated, rinse the wall with 2 mL methyl formate.
Check regularly the solvent levels.
When ~95% is evaporated, rinse the wall with 2 mL methanol.
Leave samples in TurboVap LV until all the solvent has evaporated.
Add 40 μL of methanol/water (1:1, vol/vol).
Vortex the mixture for 10 seconds.
Centrifuge samples at 2000 x g for 2 minutes at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant into borosilicate vial inserts placed in a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Centrifuge the samples at 10000 x g for 10 seconds at 4°C.
Check the vial insert for the presence of a pellet.
If no pellet is visible, transfer the insert into an injection tube.
If a pellet is visible, repeat steps 33 to 35.
Place the samples in the automated injector ASAP.
Start the LC-MS/MS system.
Keep an Agilent Poroshell 120 EC-C18 column (100 mm x 4.6 mm x 2.7 µm) at 50°C.
Maintain the initial mobile phase as methanol/water/acetic acid in a ratio of 20:80:0.01 (vol/vol/vol).
Maintain the flow rate at 0.5 mL/min.
Ramp the mobile phase to 50:50:0.01 (vol/vol/vol) over 0.5 minutes.
Ramp the mobile phase from 2 min to 11 min to 80:20:0.01 (vol/vol/vol).
Maintain the mobile phase until 14.5 min.
Ramp the mobile phase to 98:2:0.01 (vol/vol/vol) for the next 0.1 minutes.
Maintain the mobile phase at 98:2:0.01 (vol/vol/vol) for 5
Inject 35 µL of the sample.
Include in the sequence reference standards and the 100% IS (40 µL injection).
Maintain an Agilent Poroshell 120 EC-C18 column at 50°C.
Initiate mobile phase with methanol/water/acetic acid of 20:80:0.5 (vol/vol/vol).
Maintain the flow rate at 0.6 mL/min.
Ramp the mobile phase to 55:45:0.5 (vol/vol/vol) over 0.2 min.
Maintain the mobile phase for 1 min.
Ramp the mobile phase to 70:30:0.5 (vol/vol/vol) over 5min.
Ramp the mobile phase to 80:20:0.5 (vol/vol/vol) for 2 min.
Maintain the mobile phase for 3 min.
Ramp the mobile phase to 98:2:0.5 (vol/vol/vol) over 3 min.
Maintain the mobile phase for 2 min.
Inject 35 µL of the sample.
Include in the sequence reference standards and the 100% IS (40 µL injection).
Keep a Chiralpak AD-RH column at room temperature.
Initiate mobile phase with methanol/water/acetic acid 95:5:0.01 (v/v/v).
Maintain the flow rate at 0.15 mL/min.
Maintain the mobile phase for 15 min.
Inject no more than 10 µL of sample.
Operate QTrap 5500 or QTrap 6500 in negative mode.
Determine source parameters using manual tune tool from Analyst software by T-infusion of synthetic or authentic standards in phase.
Set individual MRM transitions and respective parameters using manual tune tool from Analyst software by T-infusion of synthetic or authentic standards in phase.
Select Scheduled MRM option.
Set data acquisition window to 90 seconds.
Operate QTrap 5500 or QTrap 6500 in positive mode.
Determine source parameters using manual tune tool from analyst software by T-infusion of synthetic or authentic standards in phase (see Table 5 and 6 for parameters used).

Determine individual MRM transitions and respective parameters using manual tune tool from analyst software by T-infusion of synthetic or authentic standards in phase (see Table 3 and 4 for parameters used).
Operate QTrap 5500 or QTrap 6500+ in negative mode.
Determine source parameters using manual tune tool from analyst software by T-infusion of synthetic or authentic standards in phase (see Table 1 and 2 for parameters used).
Determine MRM transitions and respective parameters using manual tune tool from analyst software by T-infusion of synthetic or authentic standards in phase.
Employ an IDA experiment to collect MS/MS spectral information from the same samples.
List parent ions of internal standards in the IDA Ion exclusion tab to minimize interference during data collection.
Set the polarity of the assay in the EPI scan window as appropriate.
Set the m/z window for ion detection in the EPI window to 100-400 for negative ion mode experiments and 100-680 for positive ion mode experiments.
Conduct analysis using Analyst software version 1.6.3.
Build a quantitation method using your standard reference mix.
Load samples using the created method.
Integrate internal standards, noting retention times of each internal standard in samples and standards.
Identify each LM by matching its retention time to synthetic or authentic standards.
Use d4-PGE2 for AA-derived prostaglandins and thromboxane.
Use d5-RvD2 and d5-LXA4 for trihydroxylated species DHA/DPA and AA/EPA-derived respectively.
Use d4-LTB4 for dihydroxylated species DHA/DPA/AA/EPA-derived.
Use d8-5S-HETE for monohydroxylated species DHA/DPA/AA/EPA-derived.
Use d5-LTC4 for glutathionyl conjugated species DHA/AA-derived.
Use d5-LTD4 for cysteinylglycinyl conjugated species DHA/AA-derived.
Use d5-LTE4 for cysteinyl conjugated species DHA/AA-derived.
Calculate the expected RT for the analytes of interest in each sample by comparing the relative retention time of the analyte with the respective internal standard in the standard mix.
Calculate recoveries by comparing the amount of each internal standard present in the samples with the amount added.
Verify that each peak has at least 4 data points and more than 2000 counts.
Integrate each LM.
Extract EPI data using Analyst Explore mode for each dataset, for each mediator.
Match the MS/MS spectrum to that of a reference standard within the same region where the peak is observed.
Ensure a positive match with at least 6 diagnostic ions matching those in the reference MS/MS spectrum, including one backbone fragment.
Proceed to quantitation using calibration curves obtained for each mediator at concentrations: 0 (blank), 0.78, 1.56, 3.12, 6.25, 12.5, 25, 50, 100 and 200 pg.
Use surrogate molecules with similar physical properties for quantitation where standards are not available.
